title: API Performance Testing: How to Design Realistic Tests
why_read: A general overview of API performance testing best practices covers useful but fairly standard ground without offering distinctive new insight.
analysis: This article walks through the basics of performance testing types, how to design realistic load scenarios, how to handle external service dependencies, and how closely test environments should mirror production. These are legitimate and practically important concerns for engineers building or validating APIs, but the content as excerpted reads as a fairly conventional overview rather than presenting novel techniques or hard data. It could serve as a decent refresher or onboarding resource for less experienced engineers. For experienced practitioners, it likely doesn't offer much beyond what's already common knowledge in the field.
